newsitem.title: USA: Heatoil retailers see demand uptick due to cold.
newsitem.headline: Heatoil retailers see demand uptick due to cold.

text.p: Heating oil retailers are seeing an increase in heating oil demand following below normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.

"We have seen demand increase, and it's about 10 percent ahead of a year ago at this time," said Arthur Chaves, treasurer of Cohen Oil, a heating oil retailer with storage capacity of 800,000 gallons in Massachusetts.
It was warmer in November last year, sharpening year ago demand comparisons, retailers said.
Weather Services Corp forecasted temperatures to be between four to 14 degrees below normal all week in the Northeast.

"There has been some increase in demand. You have to consider that it was much warmer last year when making the comparison," said Paul Vermylen, president of Meenan Oil, a large heating oil retailer in New York.
Heating oil stocks continue to be tight, with inventories 15 million barrels below year ago according to the most recent stock data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Prices are expected to continue volatile due to unpredictable weather patterns, but retailers have said they do not expect a shortage since refiners have proven they can meet demand through high production levels.
"No one is going to run out of heating oil, but there will be price volatility due to the weather," said Vermylen. -- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
